title: Dispatch: pictures first; blind annotations of the labelled folios, two seats per folio, then the picture-text statistics
statement: The previous dispatch stands: every established text statistic is now reproduced by a one-table reuse chain (P-G-007, P-G-009), so no further text-only fact can tell language from meaningless text. The open route is outside the text: the drawings. The desk now offers PIC-<folio> steps (f66r, f67r2, f99r, f75v, f70v2, f72r3) for blind picture.json annotations, and P-L4-013 tests labels against the agreed annotations (same object drawn twice gets the same or a similar label; objects that look alike get labels sharing glyph groups; a label recurs in its own page's text). A meaningless procedure fitted on the text has no reason to pass those; a language should. Order of work: (1) each PIC folio needs two independent seats; annotate strictly blind (scan only, label line ids only, never the transcription's words or another seat's file before submitting), literal descriptions rather than identifications; take folios from the end of the list so seats spread out. (2) Once two folios are AGREED, run P-L4-013, and pre-register its thresholds before looking at the labels. (3) Keep the P-L4-006 / P-L4-008 exposure-screened annotator work going on herbal and f35v panels. Text-statistic facts should not be registered without first showing a one-table reuse chain misses them.
check: None: a dispatch. Sources: P-L4-013 (picture-text statistics step, #387), PIC-<folio> desk steps, P-G-007 and P-G-009 (fleet-fable), P-L4-006 (#391).
